name: sync_basic
kind: installation from the version 1 / 2 / 4 readings, frozen before any replay with the changed engine; no new GPU data: (G1) the result of an mbarrier wait: issued at once, ready one result latency after the later of its own service start and the completion of its phase; a phase completed by a SYNCS instruction carries no release latency and no wake cost for anything that waits on it; (R2) per-SM service of the mbarrier SYNCS instructions and (R3) nanosleep by the measured requests, both word for word from version 3. bar.sync and the instruction path of the hint form are not installed
mechanisms: synchronization.mbarrier (wait result, release between warps, per-SM service)
why: Version 4 measured the hand-off between two warps with clocks: on both devices a try_wait blocked when another warp's arrive comes lets its reader issue 38.6-39.1 cycles after that arrive's issue, whatever the time it had been blocked (140-9500 cycles, across the time-out), and a try_wait issued after another warp's arrive returns as after the warp's own. That is the installed SYNCS.PHASECHK result latency (37.9) counted from the later of the two instructions. The engine instead holds the try_wait at issue until completion + 87.9 (228 / 146 for a waiter blocked at completion, 224 / 160-224 for a NANOSLEEP.SYNCS sleeper) and then adds the result latency: 126-266 where the hardware takes 38-39, and it books the wait on the try_wait while the hardware books it on the reader of its predicate.
data_seen_before_freezing: Everything listed in version 3 (its data_seen (a)-(f) stand and are part of this version) and the version 4 addendum with its tables. No replay with a changed engine.

(g) How the current replay sees the hint form (u.handoff_hint, 74ce8aab ledger): of the retry loop it keeps the last successful SYNCS.PHASECHK of each wait (failed polls are folded) and, in part of the iterations, the first TRYWAIT and the NANOSLEEP.SYNCS; the wait is semantic:mbarrier_wait at the kept check. So most hint-form waits of a replay are an ordinary mbarrier_wait row and fall under G1; a NANOSLEEP.SYNCS that is kept takes the sleeper path. Both must use the same date or the replayed time depends on what the fold kept.

rules.G1: Wait result. (i) An mbarrier_wait row that is not a known failed poll and has no deferred block issues as soon as the warp's ordinary issue conditions hold; it never waits at issue for its phase. (ii) Its result is ready at max(its own service_start (R2), the visible date of the awaited phase) + the SYNCS.PHASECHK result latency (instruction.service, unchanged). If the phase is not complete when the wait issues, the result is pending and is fixed when the phase completes; a wait whose phase never completes is a deadlock as before. (iii) The result time is put on the dependency barrier the instruction raises and on its destination, so a reader waits there (ledger reason barrier:SYNCS.PHASECHK); if the instruction raises no dependency barrier, the warp's next issue is held until the result time. (iv) Visible date of a phase. Completed by an instruction whose operation class begins with SYNCS (arrive, with or without transaction count, or expect_tx): the completion date itself (R2: the service_start of that instruction), later only by the store-visibility settle the engine already applies at a release; synchronization.mbarrier.release.cycles and suspended_wake_cycles are not added, and a NANOSLEEP.SYNCS sleeper on such a phase wakes at that date without syncs_wake_cycles; deferred blocks and failed-poll suspensions on such a phase use the same date. Completed by anything else (TMA and bulk transfers, cp.async arrivals, UTCBAR, CLC responses): the dates the engine uses today, unchanged (release = completion + cycles; completion + suspended_wake_cycles for a wait that was pending at completion; sleepers with syncs_wake_cycles) - those completions have not been measured in a hand-written kernel (TMA step).
rules.R2: Service. Each SM has one server for the SYNCS instructions that carry an mbarrier_arrive or mbarrier_wait row (operation class beginning with SYNCS; known failed polls take no turn). In issue order: service_start = max(issue cycle, server_free); server_free = service_start + service_interval_cycles. An arrive's effects are dated at its service_start (the phase completion cycle and everything derived from it); a wait's result latency counts from its service_start. Issue itself is never delayed by the server. service_interval_cycles is a new field of synchronization.mbarrier.release (cycles, scope SM, cluster-local); 0 or absent = no server and the previous timing bit for bit.
rules.R3: nanosleep. control.nanosleep.cycles becomes a piecewise-linear table over the request as the converter supplies it (ns), with the measured points below; the engine rule is unchanged (wake = issue + cycles, PTX cap 1 ms, NANOSLEEP.SYNCS and syncs_wake_cycles untouched). The axis keeps its name in this version; renaming it (requested_sleep_ns) goes with the pending pure-refactor clean-up so that this commit changes no job content besides the leaf.

leaves.synchronization.mbarrier.release.service: s = sum_i(T_i k_i) / sum_i(k_i^2) over the cells in which the server is saturated (s.mbar_self.w4, t.mbar_all.w4, t.mbar_self.w8), T_i = hardware sample total per iteration of (a), k_i = SYNCS instructions per iteration on the SM = 2 x warps. h100 (47.24 x 8 + 51.09 x 8 + 86.87 x 16) / 384 = 5.67; b300 (49.92 x 8 + 50.95 x 8 + 85.96 x 16) / 384 = 5.68. Evidence measured; sources sync_basic.h100.v2 / sync_basic.b300.v2.
leaves.control.nanosleep.cycles: points (request ns, cycles) = the clock cost per sleep of the one-warp cells (derive column 'cost', launch 2): h100 (100, 244.35) (1000, 2024.14) (10000, 31999.47) (100000, 254192.25) (1000000, 1881736.06); b300 (100, 249.33) (1000, 2064.23) (10000, 32622.53) (100000, 243709.00) (1000000, 1944673.03); and a point at 0 on the line through the first two (h100 46.60, b300 47.67) so that requests below 100 ns follow the short law instead of the 100 ns value. The table clamps above 1 ms (the PTX cap). Between 1 us and 10 us the two regimes meet at an unmeasured request: interpolation there is not evidence (no such request in either full-GPU set). Evidence measured; same sources.
leaves.unchanged: instruction.service SYNCS.PHASECHK (37.93 / 37.92: it is the hand-off), synchronization.mbarrier.release.cycles / suspended_wake_cycles and control.nanosleep.syncs_wake_cycles (kept for phases not completed by a SYNCS instruction), synchronization.cta.release.

replay: The version 1, 2 and 4 cells of both devices are replayed from their existing captures with the new formal build (clean clone, seven gates), with the issue journal, into $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/stall-attribution/sync_basic-v5/<device>; hardware columns are the existing reference passes and clock tables. Cycles per loop iteration = sum over the loop-body pcs of the ledger (version 3 (a)).

criteria.C1 (G1, own phase): s.mbar_self and t.mbar_all at one warp per CTA: replay total within 15 % of the hardware sample total (h100 27.68 / 27.99, b300 27.24 / 27.56); semantic:mbarrier_wait on the try_wait pcs at most 1 cycle per iteration; the wait sits on the readers of the try_wait predicates (barrier:SYNCS.PHASECHK) and is within 25 % of the hardware long_scoreboard there (16.96 / 18.31, 17.03 / 18.21).
criteria.C2 (R2): t.mbar_self.w2, s.mbar_self.w4, t.mbar_all.w4, t.mbar_self.w8: replay total within 15 % of the hardware sample total (h100 32.96 / 47.24 / 51.09 / 86.87, b300 31.27 / 49.92 / 50.95 / 85.96), the wait on the readers as in C1 (the hardware's mio_throttle share on the SYNCS at 8 warps is reported as not modelled).
criteria.C3 (untouched cells): s.loop*, s.bar*, s.membar*, s.mbar_trywait_fail*, u.bar*, u.bar_late*: ledger and cycles identical to the 74ce8aab replay. s.mbar_arrive*: total within 1 cycle per iteration of the 74ce8aab replay.
criteria.C4 (R3): s.sleep100, s.sleep1000 (1 and 4 warps), t.sleep10u, t.sleep100u, t.sleep1m: replay cycles per sleep within 3 % of the hardware clock cost (these are the points themselves; the check is that the request reaches the leaf in the unit the table is stated in); the wait stays where it is (suspended:sleep after the NANOSLEEP).
criteria.C5 (G1, hand-off): u.handoff.k0, .k16, .k64, .k256, .k512, both directions, from the issue journal: D = issue cycle of the waiter's first instruction after the wait row that the arrive completes (the reader of its predicate) minus the issue cycle of that arrive; median over iterations and CTAs within 3 cycles of 38.8 (hardware 38.6-39.1). u.ready.k64 and u.selfwait: the reader issues within 3 cycles of 38 after the try_wait's issue in both, and the two agree within 2. In every u.* mbarrier cell semantic:mbarrier_wait on the wait pcs is at most 1 cycle per iteration and the blocked time is on the reader.
criteria.reported, not judged: t.mbar_pingpong*, the periods of the u.* cells and u.handoff.k1024 (they hold the YIELD in front of the try_wait, BSSY / BSYNC and the S2UR reads, which belong to the branch and MIO steps); u.handoff_hint.* (the journal distance from the arrive to the loop's exit branch against the hardware's 70: the replay is expected up to 30 short, the instruction path of the hint form not being modelled).
criteria.decision: C1 or C5 failing on either device: G1 is not installed. C2 failing on a device: that device's service_interval_cycles stays 0 and the readings are reported. C4 failing on a device: that device keeps its old leaf. C3 failing: the cause is found before anything is installed. Criteria are not changed after the replays; a failed one is reported with its numbers.

full_gpu: After installation both 500-case sets are replayed with ledgers and compared (attribution, site and per-pc errors, MAPE) for the table of stall-attribution.md section 4. Reported, not a criterion. Hypotheses, not expectations to be met: waits on phases completed by another warp's arrive (producers waiting for consumers, and consumers in kernels without TMA) lose 90-230 cycles each in the replay, so replays get faster where those waits are on the critical path and the replay, already faster than hardware in most cases, may move further from the cycle counts; the wait moves from the try_wait pcs to their readers (per-pc error); cases with plain NANOSLEEP lose replay time at those sites; waits on TMA-completed phases do not change in time.
not_installed_here: bar.sync (the law for simultaneous arrival, 7.5 + 2.0 per warp per CTA up to 32 warps, is established; a late arrival with more than one warp per SMSP is not: version 4 addendum); the hint form's instruction path (predicated-off PHASECHK holding its reader 22 cycles, NANOSLEEP.SYNCS acting on the next instruction); the 1.96 microsecond try_wait time-out (replay folds failed polls); phases completed by TMA / bulk / cp.async / UTCBAR / CLC; arrive behind a lane-predicate branch (control.reconvergence floor, branch step); the bounded SYNCS queue (mio_throttle); the YIELD in front of a try_wait (branch step).
not_allowed: No value from another machine or from the literature; no full-GPU case used to choose a rule or a value.

addenda.when: 2026-11-17, full-GPU replays after installation (both 500-case sets with ledgers): full-sb5 (build 1f831181) and full-sb5b (formal build 5aa9cc49, clean clone stall-attribution-19, seven gates); a defect of the G1 implementation found by the first and fixed before the second
addenda.text: full-sb5: H100 500 / 500; B300 498 / 500, CUF-DSL-BW-C03 and -C04 ended in unsupported:engine:deadlock (both complete with build 74ce8aab). Bisection on C03 (diag-sb5-deadlock/{E1..E4}): deadlock with build 1f831181, with the same engine and the 5cf7dbd5 tree (no service interval) and with build 781a1502; none with 74ce8aab: the G1 commit. Evidence (issue journal written on the deadlock exit, commit f089ecdc; control words from the capture): the MMA warp issues two try_waits that write the same dependency barrier (write-barrier field 5), one on a barrier completed by a TMA load and one on a barrier completed later by four SYNCS arrives; both results are pending, and mbarrier_phase_complete replaced the barrier's pending marker by the first fixed result, so the reader (wait mask bit 5) issued at the first result, the warp re-filled a pipeline stage one round early and a consumer then waited on a phase that had already passed. A dependency barrier is a counter (issue_rules v1: the latest producer decides) and G1 (iii) puts the result time on the barrier: the implementation did not, with two pending results on one barrier. Fix 5aa9cc49: per barrier the number of pending results and the latest finite release among its producers; the barrier is released when the last pending result is fixed (CTest fixtures g1_two_pending, g1_two_pending_rev; CTest 16 / 16). Rules, leaves and criteria unchanged. With build 5aa9cc49: C03 16657 cycles (16800 with 74ce8aab), C04 29026; the 110 small-kernel ledgers of both devices are byte-identical to the second replay (sync_basic-v5r3 against -v5r2) and the judge scripts give the same verdicts (C1-C5 PASS on both). full-sb5b: 500 / 500 on both devices; against full-sb5 three H100 cases move by at most 0.13 % and the two B300 cases complete. Reported (not a criterion), full-sb5b against full-xu (74ce8aab): H100 attribution / site / per-pc error 0.3731 / 0.2662 / 0.7932 (0.376 / 0.284 / 0.926), MAPE 10.60 % (11.01), P90 20.4 %, median sim / hardware 0.909, 280 cases slower and 152 faster; B300 0.3599 / 0.3083 / 1.0714 (0.353 / 0.313 / 1.220), MAPE 9.50 % (9.62), P90 17.9 %, median 0.920, 269 slower and 182 faster. Against the hypotheses of `full_gpu`: the per-pc error falls on both devices (the wait moved to the readers), as expected; the replays did not get faster on the whole (the per-SM service of SYNCS and the nanosleep points outweigh the removed release latency in most cases), so that hypothesis did not hold; B300 attribution error rose by 0.007 (mbarrier_poll sites +3.4 points of residency against +3.7 before, not_selected +3.3).
